solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Made it so terrible to be nuked

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so these words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone made a situation so dreadful that it deserved to be blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the eight letters of MADE IT SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomised means broken into tiny particles, as by a nuclear blast, so it can stand for nuked.

clue.text: Religious extremism of the Middle Eastern area

parts.note: Omani means from Oman, a country of the Middle East

explanation.surface: A comment on religious fanaticism in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Theomania is a religious mania, an obsessive belief in being god-inspired: extremism of faith.

clue.text: Very much energy put into little climbing

indicators.note: a piece put into another is placed inside it
in a down entry climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: slim means slight or little, as in slim chances
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A great deal of energy goes into a small climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns SLIM into MILS, and 'put into' drops E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles is an informal intensifier: 'miles better' means very much better.

clue.text: Order issued to restrain a crowd

indicators.note: restraining something holds it in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: sent means sent out, issued
to cram is to crowd or pack in tightly

explanation.surface: An order is given so that a mob can be held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command, but it is the church sense: ordination is one of the sacraments.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Orders, ordination, is one of the Christian sacraments, so an order is an example of a sacrament.

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: still means but or nevertheless

explanation.surface: An instruction: don't put anything in, take it out instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' picks the first letters of don't and insert.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil a substance is to extract its essence by boiling and condensing, a synonym in the chemical sense.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: just means fair or ethical, which is moral

explanation.surface: Killing time is nearly what someone is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' reads as 'nearly', but 'just' is MORAL and 'about' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal blow or wound is a killing one: a fatal, deadly blow.

definitions.meaning: one's ... are one's financial resources or earnings
to mean a lot is to matter, as in 'it really matters to me'

explanation.surface: A statement that what someone earns matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Means is both a noun for financial resources and a verb for being significant to someone.

clue.text: Space station for one going up with rocket?

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station
per means for each one, as in a pound per person
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A space station fits a rocket for its launch upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns MIR and PER into REPRIM. A rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off; the space theme misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket is British informal for a sharp rebuke, the same as a reprimand.

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: aged means old
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone shivers in an old nurse's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' puts U inside AGED; the nursing uniform picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is a fever with shaking fits, so agued describes someone shivering with fever.

parts.note: to bell is to ring or call, as with a bell
OC is a common shorthand for an only child

explanation.surface: A suggestion to label a solitary child a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French writer famous for comic verse such as Cautionary Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc wrote much light verse, so a poet is a fair description of him.

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, a drink
MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician

explanation.surface: A politician goes into the bar and orders a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but is the verb meaning to put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to crush or end it, a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Agents from Spain fail to seize house

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
to miss is to fail to catch or grab
Aries is the first house of the zodiac in astrology

explanation.surface: Spanish spies fail to take over a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissaries are envoys sent on a mission, so they are agents acting for others.

indicators.note: out means out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word falls short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A motor-racing series is close to dying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the G from DYING, and 'out' rearranges DYIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy is short for IndyCar, the American open-wheel racing series, a form of motorsport.

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to be part of something is to be in it; the figure is eight, written as a word

explanation.surface: Something natural forms part of the number eight.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is just the number. 'in eight' spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn rather than learnt, so they are natural ones.

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: armies are military forces

explanation.surface: These people provide for our troops in an occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: Armouries are stores of weapons that supply troops, so they are suppliers in a military sense.

clue.text: I'll take lead in small plastic trap preparations

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside another
plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped
take means the first piece takes the next one alongside it

parts.note: the I of I'll, the speaker
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Someone will take charge of a small trap made of plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' rearranges the word small into LALMS, which IPB enters. Trap is slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for mouth, and these balms are ointments prepared to soothe the mouth's edges.

clue.text: Most spotted point that suggests cuts

indicators.note: cuts means cuts into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: implies means suggests or hints

explanation.surface: The most noticeable point is one that hints at reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots are blemishes on the skin, so the most spotted face has the most of these.

parts.note: a dash looks like the minus sign

indicators.note: awful means a mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A tiny, terrible clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash after 'Wee' is read as a minus sign; 'awful' gives CULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is Scots and informal British for tiny, a synonym for very small.

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a pal
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
TO are the last two letters of PTO, please turn over, the note at a page foot

explanation.surface: Chinese police overturn a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate. The Met is London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The palmetto is a fan palm, a type of plant.

parts.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
a crop is the fruits of the land at harvest

explanation.surface: A query about the border of a flowering fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge' is a rock outcrop, like a ridge or ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock showing at the surface, such as a ridge or crag, which can be called an edge.

clue.text: Instant retreat to a part of Italy

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A sudden escape to an Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Modena is a city and province in northern Italy, known for balsamic vinegar.

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: fraud is cheating or deception

explanation.surface: A wife who is nearly always unfaithful.
explanation.walkthrough: Frau is German for wife or Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German word for a married woman, used in English for a German wife.

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the rial is the currency, money, of Iran
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Resisting someone getting into Tehran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Tehran but means money: the rial.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival someone is to compete with them, which is to fight against them.

clue.text: This FT clue troubles user of black ink?

indicators.note: troubles means disturbs, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A clue in this newspaper vexes someone writing in black ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' rearranges THIS FT CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish squirts dark ink to escape predators, so it is a user of ink.

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A sweet tin was cleared out on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves only the first and last letters of deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for sweets or a sweet.

parts.note: far means much, as in far better
to go is to work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: An American city offers plenty of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fargo is the largest city in North Dakota.

parts.note: set is a television set; a meal from its menu is eaten in front of the screen

explanation.definitionFit: A pre-cooked tray meal eaten in front of the television, which the 'set' points to.

clue.text: Failure to drop one off results in 7

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Not removing one item leads to a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' takes I out of FAILURE and 'off' rearranges what is left. 7 is the answer to 7 Down, a rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long angry telling-off, the same as a reprimand.

clue.text: Fine soil covering a pair of spades

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece goes outside another

parts.note: clay is a heavy soil
S is short for spades in card games, so two of them give SS

explanation.surface: Good earth lies over a couple of garden spades.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy means stylish and of high quality, which is fine in its admiring sense.

clue.text: Old info on way to produce virus

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the earlier pieces follow the way

parts.note: a path is a way
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Old information along a route leads to a viral outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British informal for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathogen is any disease-causing organism, and a virus is an example.
